answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity with slashing: before an agent may earn or vote it must lock collateral, which is forfeited if two identities trace to the same controller. Verifiers at the network summit require each bond to come from a distinct funded origin, reject weak copper collateral for trusted roles, and treat a rare comet credential as proof of uniqueness. An attacker must post one full bond per fake agent and a detected farm loses them all, so cost rises linearly with Sybil size and soon exceeds any honest reward.
